definitions.explanation: A large family-controlled industrial and financial conglomerate, particularly those that dominated the Japanese economy from the Meiji era through World War II. The major zaibatsu (Mitsubishi, Mitsui, Sumitomo, Yasuda) were formally dissolved after WWII but their successor companies remain influential.

examples.japanese: {戦前|せんぜん}の{日本|にほん}は{財閥|ざいばつ}が{経済|けいざい}を{支配|しはい}していた。
examples.english: Prewar Japan's economy was dominated by zaibatsu.

examples.japanese: GHQは{財閥|ざいばつ}{解体|かいたい}を{命|めい}じた。
examples.english: GHQ ordered the dissolution of the zaibatsu.

examples.japanese: {三菱|みつびし}は{日本|にほん}を{代表|だいひょう}する{財閥|ざいばつ}の{一|ひと}つだった。
examples.english: Mitsubishi was one of Japan's most prominent zaibatsu.

notes:
USAGE:
The term {財閥|ざいばつ} is used as a loanword in English ("zaibatsu"). In modern Japanese, it sometimes appears in drama and fiction to describe wealthy, powerful families. The {四大|よんだい}{財閥|ざいばつ} (four great zaibatsu) were {三菱|みつびし}, {三井|みつい}, {住友|すみとも}, and {安田|やすだ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {財閥|ざいばつ}{解体|かいたい}: dissolution of zaibatsu
- {四大|よんだい}{財閥|ざいばつ}: the four great zaibatsu
- {財閥|ざいばつ}{系|けい}: zaibatsu-affiliated
- {財閥|ざいばつ}{企業|きぎょう}: zaibatsu company
- {新興|しんこう}{財閥|ざいばつ}: newly-risen conglomerate

SIMILAR WORDS:
In modern usage, {企業|きぎょう}グループ (corporate group) or {系列|けいれつ} (keiretsu) describes the successor structures. In Korean context, チェボル ({財閥|ざいばつ}, chaebol) uses the same kanji and refers to similar family-controlled conglomerates.
